axis_note: Pure Theta-path. EWC changes only the objective by which the deployed weight vector Theta is updated across task rounds. There is no fast-weight state W and no external store E anywhere in the paper: nothing moves at query time, nothing is retrieved, and the deployment artifact after round k is a single ordinary weight vector. The only per-task state that survives a round is two frozen vectors of the same shape as Theta (the anchor Theta* and the Fisher diagonal F), which live in the trainer, not in the served model. In the S0 three-path taxonomy this is the REGULARISATION prototype of the Theta path, standing against Deep Generative Replay (1705.08690) as the REPLAY prototype -- and the paper argues explicitly against the replay option (§1 lines 50-54).

problem_stated.statement: Neural networks trained sequentially on tasks A then B abruptly lose performance on A, because the weights important for A are changed to meet the objective of B. The paper names this catastrophic forgetting and states that it 'has been widely thought that catastrophic forgetting is an inevitable feature of connectionist models' (Abstract, lines 19-20). The paper's target is continual learning: 'the ability to learn consecutive tasks without forgetting how to perform previously trained tasks' (§1, lines 35-36).
problem_stated.why_the_obvious_fix_is_rejected: The paper explicitly rejects the interleaving/replay answer on a CAPACITY argument, not an accuracy argument: 'If tasks are presented sequentially, multitask learning can only be used if the data are recorded by an episodic memory system and replayed to the network during training. This approach (often called system-level consolidation [McClelland et al., 1995]), is impractical for learning large numbers of tasks, as in our setting it would require the amount of memories being stored and replayed to be proportional to the number of tasks.' [§1, lines 50-54]
problem_stated.constraint_the_paper_imposes_on_itself: Fixed network capacity. 'the EWC approach presented here makes use of a single network with fixed resources (i.e. network capacity) and has minimal computational overhead' [§2.2, lines 243-244]. This rules out the two other 2016 answers it cites: adding capacity (Ring 1998; Rusu et al. 2016 progressive nets) and per-task networks distilled into one (Rusu et al. 2015; Parisotto et al. 2015) [§2.2, lines 240-243].
problem_stated.biological_warrant_offered: Task-specific synaptic consolidation: enlarged dendritic spines persist across subsequent learning and their selective erasure abolishes the corresponding skill [§1, lines 58-72, citing Yang et al. 2009, Hayashi-Takagi et al. 2015, Cichon & Gan 2015, Fusi et al. 2005, Benna & Fusi 2016].

inherited_open_question.detail: The paper quotes NO prior work's stated open question. There is no sentence of the form 'X left open whether ...' anywhere in the file. Its bridge-in is a field-level gap assertion in the authors' own voice: 'little progress has been made in achieving continual learning' [§1, lines 44-45] and 'The lack of algorithms to support continual learning thus remains a key barrier to the development of artificial general intelligence' [§1, lines 54-57].
inherited_open_question.what_it_implicitly_answers_1: The empirical ceiling reported by the hyperparameter-tuning line of work. The paper characterises it: 'Previous attempts to solve the continual learning problem for deep neural networks have relied upon careful choice of network hyperparameters, together with other standard regularization methods, in order to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. However, on this task, they have only achieved reasonable results on up to two random permutations [Srivastava et al., 2013, Goodfellow et al., 2014].' [§2.1, lines 200-203]. EWC's permuted-MNIST experiment is built to break exactly that two-permutation ceiling, and the dropout+early-stopping baseline is constructed to reproduce Goodfellow et al. 2014 as faithfully as possible ('In order to replicate the results of [Goodfellow et al., 2014]', §4.1 line 526; dropout 0.2 input / 0.5 hidden as suggested there, lines 527-528; 'a similar cross-validated hyperparameter search as [Goodfellow et al., 2014]', lines 203-204). This is the closest thing to an inherited question, but it is the authors' summary of prior RESULTS, not a quotation of a prior open QUESTION.
inherited_open_question.what_it_implicitly_answers_2: The scaling objection to CLS system-level consolidation [McClelland et al. 1995]: storage proportional to the number of tasks [§1, lines 50-54]. EWC's answer is that the sufficient statistic of a past task can be two vectors of size |Theta| rather than a dataset. This is the fork that the monograph's Theta path inherits: Deep Generative Replay (1705.08690, 2017) answers the SAME objection the opposite way -- keep replay, but make the stored object a generator instead of a dataset -- and it is DGR that cites EWC, not the reverse (EWC is 2016 and cannot cite it).
inherited_open_question.what_it_implicitly_answers_3: The prior quadratic-penalty line: French & Chater 2002 (random inputs to build a quadratic approximation of the energy surface; 'Their approach is slow, as it requires re-computing the curvature at each sample') and Eaton & Ruvolo 2013 ELLA ('requires computing and inverting matrices with a dimensionality equal to the number of parameters being optimized, therefore it has been mainly applied to linear and logistic regressions') [§3, lines 342-347]. EWC's claimed delta over both is complexity: 'EWC has a run time which is linear in both the number of parameters and the number of training examples' [§3, lines 347-348].
inherited_open_question.finding_for_the_monograph: An un-inherited question at the ROOT of the Theta path. EWC opens the lineage by asserting a gap rather than by receiving one. Every later Theta-path paper in the corpus (DGR, SEAL, SCM, Nested Learning, LM Need Sleep) inherits from EWC or from its replay counterpart; EWC itself inherits from neurobiology (Yang 2009/2014, Hayashi-Takagi 2015, Fusi 2005, Benna & Fusi 2016) rather than from a machine-learning predecessor's stated problem.

core_mechanism.one_line: The experience of past rounds is not stored and not regenerated; it is compressed into a per-coordinate quadratic well around the previous solution, whose stiffness is the diagonal Fisher information, so that (U-Theta) at round k optimises only the CURRENT round's data plus a data-free spring term anchored at Theta*_{k-1}.
core_mechanism.in_frame_words: Canonical (U-Theta) is Theta_{k+1} = Theta_k - eta_Theta grad_Theta calL(R_k; Theta_k) with R_k = gen(H_k; B_s). EWC sets R_k = D_k, i.e. gen(.) DISCARDS the whole history H_{<k} and returns only the new task's data. The information about H_{<k} is re-injected not through R_k but through an added term in calL that depends on Theta alone. The sleep budget B_s is therefore spent estimating a curvature vector, not generating training samples -- this is the exact structural opposite of the replay branch.

core_mechanism.reduction_to_frame: EWC = (U-Theta) with two edits. Edit 1: gen(calH_k; B_s) returns ONLY the current round's data -- the history is deleted, not regenerated. Edit 2: calL acquires a data-free term (lambda/2) sum_i F_i (Theta_i - Theta*_i)^2 whose per-coordinate stiffness is the diagonal Fisher of the previous round. The sleep budget B_s buys a curvature estimate (Atari: 100 minibatches per task switch, Table 2 line 758-759), not synthetic training data. Nothing is written to E; nothing moves in W; the served artifact is one weight vector. Read-side equation (R) collapses to y-hat = f(q; Theta) -- W and ret(E,q) are both empty.
core_mechanism.geometric_reading_the_paper_offers: Over-parameterisation makes it likely that a solution for task B exists near the solution for task A [§2, lines 91-99]. The constraint is 'a quadratic penalty, and can therefore be imagined as a spring anchoring the parameters to the previous solution, hence the name elastic. Importantly, the stiffness of this spring should not be the same for all parameters; rather, it should be greater for those parameters that matter most to the performance during task A.' [§2, lines 103-107]. Figure 1 draws the three trajectories: unconstrained SGD (blue) destroys task A; uniform L2 (green) is too severe and prevents learning B; EWC (red) threads between them.

outer_vs_inner.readers_first_answer: Every learnable object in this paper is learned by ordinary gradient descent while the model is being TRAINED on a task, and nothing at all moves while the model is answering. EWC's 'memory' of a past task is two frozen vectors -- where the old solution was (Theta*) and how stiff each coordinate should be (F) -- both computed once, at the moment the model stops training on that task. There is no sleep phase in the sense of the rest of this corpus: the consolidation work happens AT the task boundary, inside the training loop, not in an idle period between user queries.
outer_vs_inner.which_is_the_sleep_round: The task switch. Round index k in the frame = task boundary index here. B_s is spent there and only there (snapshot Theta*, draw 100 minibatches, accumulate F). For Atari this is additionally gated: 'We only added an EWC penalty to games which had experienced at least 20 million frames' [§2.2 lines 266-267; Table 2 'start EWC 20E6', lines 718-719, 761-762].

update_layer.instantiates: (U-Theta) ONLY. One layer, one rule, no composition.
not_instantiated: (U-W): absent. There is no fast-weight state, no per-token or per-chunk update, no alpha_t retention gate, no momentum/surprise term S_t. The read equation (R) collapses to y-hat = f(q; Theta).

(U-E): absent. Nothing is written to an external store and nothing is retrieved at query time. The Atari per-task replay buffers [§2.2 lines 268-272] are TRAINING data buffers consumed by the optimiser, not a query-time store: they are never read by ret(E,q) and never influence an action except through Theta.
difference_from_canonical: calR_k is the CURRENT task's data only. gen(calH_k; B_s) is not a generator over history at all -- history is deleted. This is the defining contrast with the replay branch of the Theta path (Deep Generative Replay, 1705.08690), which keeps gen(.) and makes it parametric.

calL gains a data-free additive term, (lambda/2) sum_i F_i (Theta_i - Theta*_{k-1,i})^2 [ewc Eq. 3]. Canonical (U-Theta) has no such term. This term is what carries calH_{k-1} forward, at a cost of 2|Theta| numbers per remembered round.

F enters the OBJECTIVE, not the metric. Despite being the Fisher, EWC is not natural gradient: the update is plain first-order descent on a penalised loss (see ewc-5). The paper cites Pascanu & Bengio 2013 only for the three properties of F [§2 lines 142-146], not for a preconditioner.

The round boundary is exogenous, not scheduled by a policy. For MNIST it is fixed by the experimenter ('After a fixed amount of training on each task, however, we allowed no further training on that task's dataset', §2.1 lines 168-170). For Atari it is INFERRED at run time by the Forget-Me-Not HMM [ewc-8], which is the only part of the system that decides for itself when a round has ended.

eta_Theta is untouched by EWC. The paper's rhetoric is about 'selectively slowing down learning on the weights important for those tasks' (Abstract, lines 22-23) and 'fast learning rates on parameters that are poorly constrained by the previous tasks, and slow learning rates for those which are crucial' (§3, lines 337-339), but the IMPLEMENTATION does not modulate eta_Theta -- it adds a restoring force. The effective-learning-rate reading is an interpretation the paper offers of its own quadratic penalty, not a second mechanism.
update_layer.order_within_a_round: (1) train Theta on calR_k = task-k data under calL_EWC with the penalties accumulated from rounds j < k; (2) at the task switch, snapshot Theta*_k := Theta_k; (3) draw samples and accumulate F^{(k)} at Theta*_k (Atari: 100 minibatches from the replay buffer); (4) either append a new quadratic penalty or merge it into the running one [ewc Eq. 6 / §2 lines 158-160 -- which of the two was used is not stated]. Steps 2-4 are the entire sleep-time work.
update_layer.gating: Atari only: no penalty is created for a game until that game has been experienced for 20 million frames (= 5 million agent steps) [§2.2 lines 266-267; Table 2 lines 718-719, 761-762]. A game visited for less than 20M frames is therefore left completely unprotected.

cost_table.note_on_units: The frame's four quantities are defined for query-serving systems. EWC is a 2016 training-time algorithm with no notion of a query, a session, or a user. Three of the four cells are therefore absent as NUMBERS, but two of them are non-trivially constrained by statements the paper does make, and those statements are recorded here verbatim. Nothing below is estimated.

B_s.value: PARTIALLY PRESENT, in sample counts only (Atari); absent for MNIST.
B_s.what_is_stated: Atari: 'num. samples Fisher = 100 ... Whenever the diagonal of the Fisher is recomputed for a task, one hundred mini-batches are drawn from the replay buffer' [Table 2, lines 710-713, 758-759], with 'minibatch size = 32' [Table 2, lines 673-676]. The Fisher is recomputed 'at each task switch' [§2.2, lines 263-264]. That is the entire per-round sleep budget the paper quantifies.
B_s.arithmetic_by_this_note: 100 minibatches x 32 transitions = 3200 transitions per Fisher recomputation. This product is NOT printed in the paper; it is the multiplication of two of its stated numbers and is flagged as such.
B_s.what_is_absent: No FLOPs. No wall-clock. No GPU-hours. No energy. No MNIST Fisher-sample count (Table 1 has no Fisher row at all). No cost for the snapshot copy of Theta*. No measurement of the per-step overhead of the penalty term.
B_s.qualitative_claims_the_paper_makes_inste: 'has minimal computational overhead' [§2.2, line 244]; 'EWC has a run time which is linear in both the number of parameters and the number of training examples' [§3, lines 347-348]; 'it can be computed from first-order derivatives alone and is thus easy to calculate even for large models' [§2, lines 143-144]. All three are asymptotic or adjectival; none is measured.

L_w.detail: No latency, TTFT, throughput, ms/step or ms/token figure appears anywhere in the paper. Structurally the wake-time cost is exactly the unmodified network's forward pass: [ewc Eq. 3] modifies the training objective only, and evaluation is explicitly done with training disabled ('without allowing the agent to train on them', §2.2 lines 237-239). The one wake-time addition in the Atari system is the task-recognition module, which runs a factored-multinomial likelihood over a 42x42 downscaled frame every fourth step [Table 2 'model update period 4', 'model downscaling 2', lines 701-708] -- its cost is never measured either.
L_w.source: absence across the paper; §2.2 lines 237-239; Table 2 lines 701-708

C_cap.value: STATED AS A MULTIPLIER OF |Theta|, never in bytes.
C_cap.what_is_stated: 'With EWC, three values have to be stored for each synapse: the weight itself, its variance and its mean.' [§3, lines 369-370]. That is a 3x parameter-storage statement for the TRAINING-time state (current weight Theta, Fisher-derived variance, anchor mean Theta*).
C_cap.growth_with_task_count: Ambiguous by the paper's own construction. §2 lines 158-160 offers two options -- 'either with two separate penalties, or as one by noting that the sum of two quadratic penalties is itself a quadratic penalty' -- giving O(k|Theta|) and O(|Theta|) respectively, and never states which was used. The Atari description ('For each task, a penalty is added with anchor point given by the current value of the parameters', lines 263-265) reads as the O(k|Theta|) branch.
C_cap.what_is_absent: No byte counts. No dtype. No parameter count for either the MNIST networks or the Atari network (only shapes: 2 hidden layers of width 400, or 6 of width 100 [Table 1, lines 508-511]; conv 32/64/128 filters + 1024-unit FC [Appendix §4.2, lines 548-551]). No checkpoint size. No per-user or per-session state of any kind, because the concept does not exist in this paper.
C_cap.relative_size_hint_the_paper_gives: 'Note that this network has approximately four times as many parameters as the standard network, due to having twice as many fully connected units and twice as many filters in the final convolution.' [Appendix §4.2, lines 551-553] -- a ratio to the Mnih et al. 2015 DQN, not an absolute count.
C_cap.at_serving_time: 1x |Theta|. The anchor and the Fisher are trainer-side objects; the deployed artifact after round k is one ordinary weight vector (plus, in Atari, the per-task gains and biases of [ewc Eq. 4]).
C_cap.source: §2 lines 158-160; §2.2 lines 263-265; §3 lines 369-370; Table 1 lines 508-511; Appendix §4.2 lines 548-553

[lines 252-255 -- the label (e) is printed twice; there are six items]

True task labels vs inferred (FMN): 'The improvement here was only modest.' [line 287]. NO NUMBER.

[Table 2 lines 718-719, 761-762; main text 'We only added an EWC penalty to games which had experienced at least 20 million frames.' lines 266-267]

We trained with RMSProp, with a momentum of 0., a decay of 0.95, a learning rate of 2.5 x 10^-4, and a maximum learning rate of 2.5 x 10^-3.' [lines 630-634]

experiments.setup: A single-game DQN trained on Breakout is perturbed with zero-mean Gaussian weight noise of increasing standard deviation, drawn from three covariances: uniform (black; targets all weights equally), inverse Fisher (F + lambda I)^{-1} (blue; 'mimicking weight changes allowed by EWC'), and uniform within the nullspace of the Fisher (orange; 'targets weights that the Fisher estimates that the network output is entirely invariant to') [lines 297-302]. 'To evaluate the score, we ran the agent for ten full game episodes, drawing a new random weight perturbation for every timestep.' [lines 302-303]
experiments.headline_numbers: NONE. The result is a score-versus-sigma curve.
findings_stated: POSITIVE: 'the agent was always more robust to parameter perturbations shaped by the inverse of the diagonal of the Fisher Information (blue), as opposed to uniform perturbations (black). This validates that the diagonal of the Fisher is a good estimate of how important a certain parameter is.' [lines 311-314]

NEGATIVE, and the paper says it itself: 'Within our approximation, perturbing in the nullspace should have no effect on performance at all on performance. Empirically, however, we observe that perturbing in this space (orange) has the same effect as perturbing in the inverse Fisher space. This suggests that we are over-confident about certain parameters being unimportant: it is therefore likely that the chief limitation of the current implementation is that it under-estimates parameter uncertainty.' [lines 314-319]
Generality claim: 'Regardless of which game the agent was trained on, we observed the same patterns' [lines 310-311] -- the plotted game is Breakout only.
experiments.note: This is a self-administered falsification of half of the Fisher approximation, run on the paper's own initiative. It is the single most important experiment in the paper for the monograph's Theta-path argument, because it bounds how much of past-task structure a diagonal second-order summary can actually retain.

experiments.headline_numbers: The paper contains exactly two tables and both are hyperparameter tables: Table 1 'Hyperparameters for each of the MNIST figures' [line 515] and Table 2, whose caption ALSO reads 'Hyperparameters for each of the MNIST figures' [line 764] although its contents are the Atari settings. There is no results table. Across the entire file the only numeric performance statement is 'the total human-normalized score remains below one' for the SGD baseline [lines 282-283].
experiments.note: For a monograph chapter this is the governing fact about EWC's evidence: the claims are strong and the reported evidence is entirely graphical. Any number a later text attributes to this paper comes from re-implementations, not from here.

scale_ceiling.datasets: MNIST (28x28 grayscale handwritten digits, 10 classes) [LeCun et al. 1998, §2.1 lines 171-172] under fixed random pixel permutations, and Atari 2600 via the Arcade Learning Environment [Bellemare et al. 2013, line 232]. Nothing else. No ImageNet, no text, no language model, no sequence model of any kind.
scale_ceiling.task_sequence_length: MNIST: NEVER STATED as a number. Figure 2A uses three permutations (A, B, C) [Fig. 2 caption, line 184]; Figure 2B's task count is unlabelled in the text. Atari: exactly 10 games per experiment [lines 234-235, 582-586]. The largest task count stated numerically anywhere in the paper is therefore 10.
scale_ceiling.model_size: NO PARAMETER COUNT IS GIVEN. Only shapes. MNIST: fully-connected ReLU nets of 2 hidden layers x 400 units, 2 x 400-2000, or 6 x 100 [Table 1, lines 484-515]. Atari: conv(8,4,32) - conv(4,2,64) - conv(3,1,128) - FC(1024), stated only as 'approximately four times as many parameters as the standard network' of Mnih et al. 2015 [Appendix §4.2, lines 548-553].
scale_ceiling.token_count: N/A. No tokens, no sequences. Data volume is stated only as training duration: MNIST 20 or 100 epochs per dataset [Table 1]; Atari 50 x 10^6 frames as the pool-selection criterion for standalone DQN [line 584], with the EWC penalty gated at 20 x 10^6 frames per game [Table 2 lines 718-719].
scale_ceiling.compute: NOT STATED. No FLOPs, no GPU-hours, no wall-clock, no hardware description anywhere in the file.
scale_ceiling.sleep_budget_ceiling: The largest quantified consolidation job in the paper is 100 minibatches of 32 transitions (Atari Fisher recomputation, once per task switch) [Table 2 lines 710-713, 673-676].
scale_ceiling.seeds_and_averaging: MNIST: number of seeds not stated; 50 hyperparameter combinations searched where a range is given [lines 536-537]. Atari: 10 sets of 10 games x 4 random seeds [lines 585-586].
scale_ceiling.summary: Largest demonstration: a 10-game sequential Atari agent built on a ~4x-enlarged DQN, plus permuted-MNIST MLPs of at most 2000 units wide. Model scale is roughly six to seven orders of magnitude below any deployed language model in this corpus, the task boundary structure is either experimenter-imposed (MNIST) or inferred from raw pixels by a Dirichlet model (Atari), and no consolidation cost, latency, byte count, or forgetting rate is measured. The paper's contribution to the monograph is a MECHANISM and a licence (Eq. 2), not a quantitative scaling result.

new.definition: An algorithm that 'slows down learning on certain weights based on how important they are to previously seen tasks' by adding a per-parameter quadratic penalty anchored at the previous task's solution, with stiffness given by the diagonal Fisher information.

new.term: the elastic-spring reading of a quadratic penalty
new.definition: 'This constraint is implemented as a quadratic penalty, and can therefore be imagined as a spring anchoring the parameters to the previous solution, hence the name elastic.' The stiffness is per-parameter, not global.

The diagonal of the Fisher information matrix taken as the precision of a Laplace-approximated posterior over the past task's parameters, with three stated properties: second derivative near a minimum, computable from first-order derivatives, positive semi-definite.
The frozen snapshot of the weight vector at a task switch, around which the quadratic well is centred.

1 - d_F^2 between two tasks' unit-trace Fisher matrices, a [0,1] measure of whether two tasks depend on the same weights; used to ask whether a network subdivides its capacity or shares representations.

new.term: task-recognition as a separate, non-gradient module
new.definition: An HMM over categorical task contexts with Dirichlet-multinomial pixel emission models, grown non-parametrically via the Forget-Me-Not process, supplying the task label the consolidation machinery needs.
A small per-task parameter slice (additive bias and multiplicative gain per layer) grafted onto an otherwise shared network.
The paper's own capacity accounting for EWC: weight, variance, mean -- offered as a bridge to neurobiology (early-phase vs late-phase plasticity, short-term plasticity carrying variance).

extended_or_renamed.note: SPLIT. The paper explicitly contrasts SYSTEM-LEVEL consolidation ('the data are recorded by an episodic memory system and replayed to the network during training ... often called system-level consolidation [McClelland et al., 1995]', lines 50-53) with SYNAPTIC consolidation ('reducing the plasticity of synapses that are vital to previously learned tasks', lines 85-86). EWC claims the second. The monograph's Theta path forks exactly here, and the STC corpus's later 'consolidation' usage descends from the first branch, not the second.

Redefined operationally as an effective per-coordinate learning rate: 'This enables fast learning rates on parameters that are poorly constrained by the previous tasks, and slow learning rates for those which are crucial.' [§3, lines 337-339]. But no learning rate is actually modulated in the implementation -- see update_layer.difference_from_canonical.

Used in two incompatible senses in the same paper. (i) Parameter budget: 'a single network with fixed resources (i.e. network capacity)' [line 244]. (ii) An allocatable resource that tasks compete for: 'the constraint protects all weights equally, leaving little spare capacity for learning on B' [lines 195-196]; 'EWC allows the network to effectively squeeze in more functionality into a network with fixed capacity' [lines 208-209]. Sense (ii) is the ancestor of the corpus's C_cap discussions, but the paper never quantifies it.

The paper's own two-timescale statement, and the closest it comes to the corpus's multi-timescale framing: 'the overall system has memory on two time-scales: over short time-scales, the experience replay mechanism allows learning in DQN to be based on the interleaved and uncorrelated experiences [Mnih et al., 2015]. At longer time scales, know-how across tasks is consolidated by using EWC.' [§2.2, lines 269-273]. NOTE: neither timescale is the frame's W layer -- the short scale here is a data buffer, not a fast-weight state.

retired_or_argued_against.term: system-level consolidation / stored-and-replayed episodic memory as the answer to forgetting
retired_or_argued_against.note: Argued to be impractical because storage scales with the number of tasks [§1, lines 50-54]. This is the claim Deep Generative Replay (1705.08690) is built to defeat by making the store parametric. The monograph should present these two as the two answers to one question, with EWC's rejection quoted.

retired_or_argued_against.term: adding capacity per task (progressive networks) and per-task networks distilled into one
retired_or_argued_against.note: Not retired but explicitly declined as the comparison class: 'previous reinforcement learning approaches to continual learning have either relied on either adding capacity to the network [Ring, 1998, Rusu et al., 2016] or on learning each task in separate networks, which are then used to train a single network that can play all games [Rusu et al., 2015, Parisotto et al., 2015]. In contrast, the EWC approach presented here makes use of a single network with fixed resources' [§2.2, lines 240-244]. Neither is run as a baseline.
The claim the paper sets out to overturn: 'it has been widely thought that catastrophic forgetting is an inevitable feature of connectionist models' [Abstract, lines 19-20].

open_questions.q: How to replace the diagonal Laplace point estimate with a better posterior. The paper names this as its own principal weakness and names the successor it expects: 'our use of a point estimate of the posterior's variance (as in a Laplace approximation) does constitute a significant weakness (see Fig 4C). Our initial explorations suggest that one might improve on this local estimate by using Bayesian neural networks [Blundell et al., 2015].'
open_questions.bridge_out: The direct handle for the monograph's Theta-path chapter: EWC's own stated frontier is the QUALITY of the compressed representation of past experience, i.e. how much of calH_{k-1} survives compression into 2|Theta| numbers.

open_questions.q: How to stop under-estimating parameter uncertainty. 'it is therefore likely that the chief limitation of the current implementation is that it under-estimates parameter uncertainty.'
open_questions.bridge_out: The empirical version of the same question, and the one with evidence attached (Fig. 3C nullspace result).

open_questions.q: How to close the residual gap to independently trained networks. 'it does not reach the score that would have been obtained by training ten separate DQNs'.
open_questions.bridge_out: Defines the ceiling that every later Theta-path method is implicitly measured against; the paper leaves the gap unquantified.

open_questions.q: Whether the per-task penalties should be kept separate or merged as the task count grows. The paper offers both and decides neither: 'This can be enforced either with two separate penalties, or as one by noting that the sum of two quadratic penalties is itself a quadratic penalty.'
open_questions.bridge_out: This is the C_cap question of the Theta path in its earliest form -- O(|Theta|) versus O(k|Theta|) retained state.

open_questions.q: Whether task identity can be inferred reliably in the general unlabelled setting. Posed in the motivation -- 'the sequence of tasks may not be explicitly labelled, tasks may switch unpredictably, and any individual task may not recur for long time intervals' -- and only partly answered: giving the agent the TRUE labels instead of the inferred ones yields an improvement that 'was only modest'.
open_questions.bridge_out: Note the direction: the small gap means task inference was not the bottleneck in this setting, so the open question is whether that holds when tasks are less visually distinct than Atari games.

open_questions.q: Whether the number of tasks can grow without bound. The Forget-Me-Not guarantee is explicitly conditional: 'a time decaying switch rate alpha = 1/t guarantees good worst case asymptotic performance provided the number of tasks grows as o(n / log n)'. The condition is stated and never tested.
open_questions.bridge_out: A scaling condition on the ROUND COUNT, of the same species as the corpus's later questions about repeated sleep rounds.

open_questions.q: What the computational benefit of sampling from the weight posterior would be. 'While we do not explore the computational benefits of sampling from a posterior here, our work aligns with the notion that weight uncertainty should inform learning rates.'

Whether the algorithm feeds back into neuroscience -- specifically whether the three quantities EWC needs per synapse (weight, variance, mean) map onto short-term plasticity, early-phase plasticity and late-phase/consolidated plasticity respectively. Offered as a hypothesis, not a result.
IMPLICIT, never posed: whether EWC composes with replay or with capacity growth. The paper positions itself as an ALTERNATIVE to both [§2.2 lines 240-244] and never runs the composition.
open_questions.bridge_out: The monograph's Theta-path chapter should note that the regularisation/replay fork was never tested as a union in the originating paper of either branch.

open_questions.q: IMPLICIT, never posed: where the boundary between shared body and per-task slice should sit. The Atari system hand-picks 'biases and per element multiplicative gains' as the per-task parameters; no study of the choice is offered.

IMPLICIT, never posed: what the consolidation actually COSTS. Every cost statement in the paper is asymptotic ('linear in both the number of parameters and the number of training examples') or adjectival ('minimal computational overhead'); none is measured.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper contains NO results table and NO reported accuracy or score value for EWC. Its only two tables are hyperparameter tables. The single numeric performance statement in the entire file describes the BASELINE: with plain gradient descent 'the total human-normalized score remains below one'. Every EWC claim rests on a curve.
unfavorable_facts.source: Table 1 line 515; Table 2 line 764; §2.2 lines 281-283; whole-file absence

unfavorable_facts.fact: The headline scaling claim -- 'EWC allows a large number of tasks to be learned in sequence, with only modest growth in the error rates' -- never states how many tasks. The task count of Figure 2B appears nowhere in the text, and neither 'a large number' nor 'modest growth' is quantified.

The paper falsifies half of its own approximation and says so. Perturbing weights inside the Fisher's NULLSPACE -- which under the approximation should be free -- degrades performance as much as perturbing along the inverse Fisher. 'This suggests that we are over-confident about certain parameters being unimportant: it is therefore likely that the chief limitation of the current implementation is that it under-estimates parameter uncertainty.'

EWC does not reach the performance of independently trained networks, and the size of the shortfall is never quantified: 'it does not reach the score that would have been obtained by training ten separate DQNs (see Figure 1 in Appendix 4.2)'. The cross-reference is also broken -- Appendix 4.2 contains Figure 4, not Figure 1.

The Atari result confounds EWC with at least five other simultaneous changes to the reference agent, and NO ablation isolates the EWC penalty: '(a) a network with more parameters, (b) a smaller transition table, (c) task-specific bias and gains at each layer, (d) the full action set in Atari, (e) a task-recognition model, and (e) the EWC penalty.' The enlarged network alone has 'approximately four times as many parameters as the standard network'.

The Atari system keeps stored experience -- 'separate short-term memory buffers for each inferred task' -- which partially reinstates the very stored-and-replayed-memory approach the paper rejects in its introduction as 'impractical for learning large numbers of tasks'. The buffers scale with the number of inferred tasks.

Internal numerical inconsistency in the Atari setup: the main text reports 'a smaller replay buffer (5 x 10^5 past experiences)' while Table 2 lists 'memory size 50000' glossed as 'The replay memory stores the last fify thousand transitions experienced'. The two differ by a factor of ten.

The vendored v2 is demonstrably a pre-final draft: Table 2's caption reads 'Hyperparameters for each of the MNIST figures' although its contents are the Atari hyperparameters; Table 1's columns are headed 'Reference figure 3A/3B/3C' and §4.1 says 'the three graphs in Figure 3 of the main text' although the MNIST figure in this text is Figure 2; the Discussion writes '(see Fig 4C)' for what the main text calls Figure 3C; §2.2 contains the unresolved LaTeX reference 'Appendix app:atari'; and the list of agent differences labels two items '(e)'.

The MNIST value of lambda -- the single hyperparameter that trades new-task learning against old-task retention -- is never stated. Table 1 has no lambda row. Only the Atari value (400) is given, and it was chosen by hyperparameter search.

The MNIST arms are not run under matched settings. Table 1 shows the EWC/L2/SGD comparison (column 3A) at lr 1e-3, no dropout, no early stopping, 2x400, 20 epochs; the dropout baseline comparison (column 3B) at lr 1e-5-1e-3, dropout yes, early stopping yes, 2x(400-2000), 100 epochs; and the Fisher-overlap study (column 3C) at 6x100, 100 epochs. Depth, width, epoch budget and regularisation all differ between the figures.

The benchmark is at the benign end of continual learning and the paper says why in its own words: the permutations change only the input encoding, not the label space. 'even for the large permutations, the layers of the network closer to the output are indeed being reused for both tasks. This reflects the fact that the permutations make the input domain very different, but the output domain (i.e. the class labels) is shared.'

Only two baselines are run on MNIST -- uniform L2 and SGD with dropout + early stopping. No rehearsal/replay baseline, no joint-training upper bound (only a 'single task' dashed line), and no comparison against the progressive-networks or per-task-network-plus-distillation approaches that §2.2 cites as the alternatives.

In Atari the EWC penalty is disabled for the first 20 million frames of every game: 'We only added an EWC penalty to games which had experienced at least 20 million frames.' A game revisited for less than that is left entirely unprotected, and no experiment varies this gate.

The multi-task form of the algorithm is left undetermined. §2 offers separate per-task penalties OR a single merged quadratic and never says which was used in the experiments. The two forms have different retained-state costs -- O(k|Theta|) versus O(|Theta|) -- so the paper does not pin down its own capacity behaviour.
unfavorable_facts.source: §2 lines 158-160; §2.2 lines 263-265 (Atari phrasing implies the per-task form)

unfavorable_facts.fact: The Fisher estimator is never written down. The paper states only that F is 'the diagonal of the Fisher information matrix' that 'can be computed from first-order derivatives alone', with no formula, no statement of whether labels are taken from the data (empirical Fisher) or sampled from the model (true Fisher), and no statement of the distribution it is averaged over. The choice materially changes the algorithm.

In Atari the Fisher is estimated from the replay buffer -- 'one hundred mini-batches are drawn from the replay buffer' -- i.e. from a stale, off-policy, per-task data distribution rather than from the task's own on-policy distribution. The paper does not remark on this or test sensitivity to the sample count.

The generality claim for the perturbation study rests on a single plotted game. 'Regardless of which game the agent was trained on, we observed the same patterns' -- but Figure 3C shows Breakout only, and no per-game data for the other games is provided for this probe.

The task-recognition module's theoretical justification is conditional and untested: alpha = 1/t 'guarantees good worst case asymptotic performance provided the number of tasks grows as o(n / log n)'. The paper never checks that its experiments satisfy the condition, and the condition itself bounds how fast task count may grow.

Every cost claim is unmeasured. 'minimal computational overhead' and 'a run time which is linear in both the number of parameters and the number of training examples' are the only cost statements, with no FLOPs, no wall-clock, no memory footprint and no energy anywhere in the paper. The one storage fact -- 'three values have to be stored for each synapse' -- appears in the Discussion as a bridge to neurobiology, not as a cost accounting.

No parameter counts are reported for any model in the paper, so the '3 values per synapse' storage claim cannot be converted into bytes from the paper alone, and the Atari network is described only relative to another paper's network ('approximately four times as many parameters as the standard network').

No variance or error bars are described for the MNIST results, and no seed count is stated for them. The Atari results are averaged over 10 sets of 10 games and 4 seeds, but the text describes no dispersion measure.

The Abstract's mechanism description does not match the implementation. 'Our approach remembers old tasks by selectively slowing down learning on the weights important for those tasks' describes a per-coordinate learning-rate modulation; [ewc Eq. 3] adds a restoring force to the loss and leaves eta_Theta untouched. The slow-learning-rate reading is an interpretation of the penalty's effect, not a second mechanism.
unfavorable_facts.source: Abstract lines 22-23; §3 lines 335-339 versus [ewc Eq. 3] lines 147-157

unfavorable_facts.fact: Scale. The largest models are a ~4x-enlarged DQN and MLPs of at most 2000 hidden units; the longest task sequence stated numerically is 10; there is no sequence model, no language model, and no notion of a query, a session or a user anywhere in the paper. The monograph's serving reader is being asked to inherit a mechanism validated six to seven orders of magnitude below deployment scale.

The description of the SGD failure mode in §2.1 has its two task labels swapped as printed: 'At the point at which the training regime switches from training on the first task (A) to training on the second (B), the performance for task B falls rapidly, while for task A it climbs steeply.' The intended statement is plainly the reverse. A monograph quoting this sentence verbatim would propagate the error.

cross_path_citations.verdict: EWC is chronologically upstream of all three paths as this corpus defines them, so 'silence' must be read carefully. What is establishable from the 42-entry bibliography: the Theta path is present (this paper is its regularisation root), the E path is completely absent, and the W path is absent ALGORITHMICALLY but present BIOLOGICALLY -- the Discussion argues for multi-timescale synaptic state in neuroscience terms and never converts it into a mechanism.

Theta_path.engaged: Yes -- this paper is the Theta path's regularisation root, and it names its competitors within the path.
citations: McCloskey & Cohen 1989; Ratcliff 1990; French 1999; McClelland et al. 1995 -- the catastrophic-forgetting problem statement [§1 lines 39-40]
Goodfellow et al. 2014; Srivastava et al. 2013 -- the hyperparameter/regularisation line whose two-permutation ceiling EWC targets [§2.1 lines 200-204]
French & Chater 2002; Eaton & Ruvolo 2013 (ELLA) -- the prior quadratic-penalty line, dismissed on cost grounds [§3 lines 342-347]
Ring 1998; Rusu et al. 2016 (progressive networks) -- capacity-growth alternative, declined [§2.2 lines 240-242]
Rusu et al. 2015 (policy distillation); Parisotto et al. 2015 (actor-mimic) -- per-task networks distilled into one, declined [§2.2 lines 240-243]

MacKay 1992 (Laplace approximation); Eskin et al. 2004 (Laplace propagation); Pascanu & Bengio 2013 (natural gradient / Fisher properties); Blundell et al. 2015 (Bayesian neural networks) -- the machinery and the named successor [§2 lines 137-146; §3 lines 352-356]

E_path.engaged: No. Zero engagement, and the paper argues against the E path's central premise.
E_path.evidence: grep over the file finds no occurrence of 'retriev', 'memory-augmented', 'neural turing', 'offline', or any vector/graph/text store. The only two external-store-shaped citations are (i) McClelland et al. 1995 system-level consolidation via 'an episodic memory system' [§1 lines 50-53], introduced solely in order to be rejected as impractical, and (ii) Mnih et al. 2015 experience replay [§2.2 lines 269-272], which is a training data buffer sampled by the optimiser and never read at action time.
E_path.note: The rejection sentence is the load-bearing one for the monograph: 'it would require the amount of memories being stored and replayed to be proportional to the number of tasks' [§1 lines 53-54]. EWC's whole design is the refusal to keep a store. The E path of this corpus is precisely the decision to keep one, and to pay the retrieval cost at query time.

W_path.engaged: Algorithmically: no. Biologically: yes, and explicitly.
W_path.algorithmic_silence: grep finds no 'fast weight', no 'meta-learn'/'meta learn', no MAML, no LSTM, no 'test-time', no transformer, no attention. There is no inner loop, no per-token or per-chunk state, and no eta_t anywhere in the paper. The word 'recurrent' occurs only inside the title of the Mante et al. 2013 neuroscience reference. Ba et al. 2016 ('Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past', NIPS 2016) is contemporaneous and is not cited.
W_path.biological_engagement: The Discussion runs a genuine multi-timescale-weight argument in neuroscience vocabulary: 'With EWC, three values have to be stored for each synapse: the weight itself, its variance and its mean. Interestingly, synapses in the brain also carry more than one piece of information. For example, the state of the short-term plasticity could carry information on the variance [Aitchison and Latham, 2015, Pfister et al., 2010]. The weight for the early phase of plasticity [Clopath et al., 2008] could encode the current synaptic strength, whereas the weight associated with the late-phase of plasticity or the consolidated phase could encode the mean weight.' [§3 lines 369-375]. Fusi et al. 2005 (cascade models of synaptically stored memories) and Benna & Fusi 2016 (computational principles of synaptic memory consolidation) are cited in the same register [§1 lines 68-72].
W_path.finding_for_the_monograph: The W layer appears in the Theta path's root paper only as biology. EWC has the ingredients of a two-timescale weight state -- a slow consolidated mean and a fast current value -- and declines to make the fast component a computational object. That refusal is exactly what the W path later takes up, and it is not framed here as an open question.

sleep_and_bio.engaged: Heavily, as the paper's rhetorical spine.
sleep_and_bio.the_sleep_finding: The word 'sleep' occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the entire file, inside the title of a cited reference: Yang, Lai, Cichon, Ma, Li & Gan, 'Sleep promotes branch-specific formation of dendritic spines after learning', Science 344(6188):1173-1178, 2014 [lines 480-481], cited only as part of the spine-persistence cluster at §1 line 61. The paper has no idle phase, no offline phase, and no sleep concept of its own: consolidation happens AT the task switch, inside the training loop. For a monograph on sleep-time compute this is the sharpest possible statement of what EWC is and is not -- the ancestor of the Theta path cites the sleep literature and builds no sleep phase.
sleep_and_bio.cls_note: McClelland et al. 1995 -- the CLS paper listed as a common ancestor in S0 §3.1 -- IS cited here (lines 40, 52-53, 443), but as the source of the system-level-consolidation proposal that the paper rejects, not as a two-systems theory to be implemented. Contrast with Deep Generative Replay (1705.08690), which does not cite McClelland 1995 at all yet builds the CLS architecture. The two ancestors of the Theta path relate to CLS in exactly opposite ways.

cross_path_citations.who_cites_whom_in_the_corpus: EWC (Dec 2016) predates every other paper in the STC corpus except CLS 1995. It cites none of them and cannot. The direction of the bridge chain is therefore forward-only from this note: Deep Generative Replay (May 2017) is the paper that answers EWC's anti-replay argument, and it is DGR that must carry the citation. The monograph's bridge-in for the DGR chapter should quote EWC §1 lines 50-54.

systems_implications.decode_cost: UNCHANGED, exactly. [ewc Eq. 3] modifies the training objective only; the served network is the same function it would have been without EWC, and evaluation is explicitly run with training disabled ('without allowing the agent to train on them', §2.2 lines 237-239). Read equation (R) collapses to y-hat = f(q; Theta): no W term, no ret(E,q) term. This is EWC's defining systems property and the reason it is the cheapest possible Theta-path write from a serving perspective. [grounded]
systems_implications.bytes_moved_per_token_or_session: ZERO per token, ZERO per session, ZERO per user. There is no per-request state of any kind in this paper -- no KV-like structure, no fast-weight tensor, no retrieved records, no per-user delta. The only quantity that scales with anything is trainer-side. [grounded: no per-query object exists anywhere in the file]
systems_implications.training_side_traffic: Per optimiser step the penalty adds one elementwise read of F and one of Theta*, plus one fused multiply-add over the parameter vector -- 2|Theta| extra element reads per step on top of the gradient. That is a bandwidth-bound AXPY, not a FLOP-bound operation, so on modern accelerators EWC's steady-state cost is a memory-bandwidth tax on the optimiser, not a compute tax. [INFERENCE by this note, from the form of ewc-5; the paper states only the asymptotics, 'a run time which is linear in both the number of parameters and the number of training examples', §3 lines 347-348]
systems_implications.trainer_memory_footprint: 3x |Theta| for the consolidation state: 'three values have to be stored for each synapse: the weight itself, its variance and its mean' [§3 lines 369-370] -- i.e. Theta, F, Theta*. In the per-task-penalty form of [ewc Eq. 6] this becomes |Theta| + 2k|Theta| after k rounds; in the merged form it stays 3|Theta|. The paper never states which form it used, so the trainer footprint of its own experiments is undetermined. [grounded on the 3-values statement and §2 lines 158-160; the k-scaling arithmetic is this note's]
systems_implications.no_byte_figure_is_derivable: The paper gives no parameter count and no dtype anywhere, so '3 values per synapse' cannot be converted to bytes from this file. Any byte figure in the monograph must be marked as the monograph's own arithmetic over an assumed dtype and an assumed model size. [grounded: absence]
systems_implications.batching_consequences: Shared-weight batching survives INTACT for the MNIST setting -- there is one weight vector, and requests from different tasks run in the same batch on the same weights. This is the sharpest contrast in the whole corpus with per-user Theta deltas: EWC pays for continual learning in accuracy headroom, not in batching. The Atari system dents this: [ewc Eq. 4] gives every layer per-game additive biases and per-element multiplicative gains, so serving mixed tasks requires selecting a per-task parameter slice by the inferred label z. The slice is small relative to the conv/FC weights but the paper never states its size. [grounded on Eq. 4 and lines 273-275; the batching translation is this note's]
systems_implications.where_the_sleep_traffic_lands: The consolidation job is: (i) copy Theta to Theta* -- one |Theta| sequential write; (ii) run 100 minibatches of 32 forward+backward passes and accumulate a squared-gradient-shaped vector [Table 2 lines 710-713, 673-676]. Both are dense, embarrassingly batchable, and touch no external storage. Against millions of training steps this is negligible, which is what 'minimal computational overhead' [line 244] means operationally. Compare the replay branch, whose sleep budget scales with the volume of synthetic data generated. [Fisher-sample numbers grounded; the batchability and the negligibility comparison are this note's inference]
systems_implications.memory_hierarchy: F and Theta* are dense vectors of exactly the parameter shape and would live in HBM alongside the optimiser moments -- functionally they are two extra optimiser slots. Nothing spills to DRAM or disk; nothing is a database. [INFERENCE by this note; the paper describes no hardware at all]
systems_implications.the_cost_structure_fork_this_paper_defin: EWC moves PARAMETERS; replay moves DATA. EWC's remembering cost is O(|Theta|) bytes and O(|Theta|) elementwise ops per step, independent of how much experience is being remembered. The replay branch's cost is O(samples generated) FLOPs and grows with the volume of experience the round must cover. That is the fork the monograph's Part III cost analysis inherits, and it is fully determined by mechanism -- neither paper measures it. [INFERENCE, but the mechanisms are grounded: §1 lines 50-54 for the storage argument, [ewc Eq. 3] for the parameter-side cost]
systems_implications.what_a_serving_engineer_can_actually_tak: One structural fact and one warning. The fact: a Theta-path method can be built whose entire retained state is two vectors the size of the model and whose serving cost is identically zero -- deployment artifact unchanged, batching unchanged, no per-user state. The warning: Figure 3C says that this compression discards more than its own theory predicts (nullspace perturbations hurt as much as inverse-Fisher ones), and the paper reports no number for what that costs in accuracy. There is no measured latency, throughput, byte count or forgetting rate in this paper to plan against.
